_howto: This file drives parkatlas.io/gear. Edit it, then run `node web/build-gear.mjs` (or `npm run web:build`) and push.
tag: your Amazon Associates tracking ID (Associates Central → top-right). Every link gets it automatically.
Per item: `asin` (preferred — the 10-char code in an Amazon product URL, e.g. B07XYZ1234) OR `search` keywords as a fallback. `url` overrides both if you paste a full SiteStripe link.
pick: true adds the personal badge. image: optional URL for a product photo; leave off for the icon-only card.
Set enabled: false on an item or section to hide it without deleting it.

hero.title: Gear worth bringing along.
hero.lede: Things I use, recommend, or would genuinely pack for a park trip. Nothing here is filler.

trust: I only include gear I use myself, have researched, or would genuinely recommend for a park trip.
disclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

sections.title: What I actually use
sections.blurb: The short list. If I'm heading out for a weekend, these are already in the car.

items.name: Nitecore NU25 headlamp
items.why: Lightweight, rechargeable, and easy to throw in a daypack without thinking about it.

items.name: Osprey Daylite Plus
items.why: Twenty liters, sits flat against your back, and the water bottle pockets actually fit a Nalgene.

items.name: Anker 10,000 mAh power bank
items.why: Two full phone charges. Enough for a weekend of photos and offline maps.

items.name: Hydro Flask 32 oz wide mouth
items.why: Ice at the trailhead is still ice at the car.

items.name: National Parks Passport
items.why: The cancellation stamps are half the fun. Every visitor center has one.

items.name: Nocs Provisions 8x25 binoculars
items.why: Small enough to leave in the glovebox, sharp enough for bighorn on a far ridge.

sections.title: Day hiking essentials
sections.blurb: The stuff that makes a five-mile loop pleasant instead of a slog.

items.name: Daypack (18–25 L)
items.why: Room for water, layers, snacks, and a first aid kit — nothing more.

items.name: Hydration bladder
items.why: You drink more when you don't have to stop to do it.

items.name: Trekking poles
items.why: Knees on the descent will thank you. Collapsible ones fit in a carry-on.

items.name: Headlamp
items.why: Sunrise hikes and late finishes. Never rely on your phone flashlight.

items.name: Portable charger
items.why: Offline maps and photos eat batteries faster than you'd think.

items.name: Compact first aid kit
items.why: Blister care and tweezers get used more than anything else.

items.name: Mineral sunscreen
items.why: High elevation sun is not the sun you're used to.

items.name: Lightweight rain shell
items.why: Afternoon thunderstorms are a feature of the mountain West, not a bug.

sections.title: National park road trip gear
sections.blurb: Parks are far apart. The drive is part of the trip — make the car work for you.

items.name: USB-C car charger
items.why: Fast enough to charge two phones while navigating.

items.name: Hard cooler
items.why: Holds ice for days between towns with grocery stores.

items.name: Seat-back organizer
items.why: Snacks, maps, and sunscreen stop living on the floor.

items.name: Binoculars
items.why: Wildlife pullouts are a lot better when you can actually see the wildlife.

items.name: Offline GPS / satellite messenger
items.why: Cell service ends at most park boundaries. This doesn't.

items.name: Roadside emergency kit
items.why: Jumper cables and a tire inflator, for the gas station that's 90 miles away.
items.search: roadside emergency kit with jumper cables

items.name: Travel blanket
items.why: Sunrise overlooks are cold. Picnics are nicer on it than on gravel.

sections.title: Camping favorites
sections.blurb: Car-camping comfort without hauling the whole garage.

items.name: Camp light
items.why: Soft, rechargeable, hangs from the tent loop.

items.name: Sleeping pad
items.why: The single biggest upgrade to sleeping outside.

items.name: Camp chair
items.why: Low, light, and packs down to the size of a water bottle.

items.name: Portable stove
items.why: Coffee in ten minutes. Every morning.

items.name: Coffee setup
items.why: A pour-over dripper and a hand grinder. Non-negotiable.

items.name: Dry bags
items.why: Clothes stay dry, and dirty ones stay contained.

items.name: Camp kitchen basics
items.why: One pot, one pan, a spatula, and a sponge in a mesh bag.

sections.title: Park passport & journaling
sections.blurb: The paper side of remembering where you've been.

items.name: National Parks Passport
items.why: Collect cancellation stamps at every visitor center.

items.name: Stamp set & stickers
items.why: The annual stamp sets slot right into the passport.

items.name: Park journal
items.why: A page per park: date, trail, weather, who you were with.

items.name: Scratch-off national parks map
items.why: Wall version of your ParkAtlas ring.

items.name: Field notebook
items.why: Waterproof pages for the trail.

items.name: Map case
items.why: Keeps the paper map you swore you'd never need dry.

sections.title: Dog adventure gear
sections.blurb: Most park roads and campgrounds welcome dogs. Trails vary — check before you go.

items.name: Collapsible water bowl
items.why: Clips to the pack. Used at every stop.

items.name: Dog water bottle
items.why: One bottle for both of you.

items.name: Long leash
items.why: Room to sniff, still on-leash where the rules say so.

items.name: Seat protector
items.why: Red dirt and wet dog, contained.

items.name: Portable dog bed
items.why: Rolls up; gives them a spot at camp.

items.name: Paw protection
items.why: Hot sandstone and sharp lava rock are hard on paws.

items.name: Waste-bag holder
items.why: Because you will forget otherwise.

sections.title: Cold weather & desert
sections.blurb: Small things that change whether you're comfortable at 9,000 ft or 105°F.

items.name: Hand warmers
items.why: Sunrise at Bryce in October. Enough said.

items.name: Neck gaiter
items.why: Sun, wind, dust, or cold — it does all four.

items.name: Cooling towel
items.why: Soak, wring, wear. Desert hikes get easier.

items.name: Wide-brim sun hat
items.why: Ears and neck are the first to burn.

items.name: Electrolyte packets
items.why: Water alone isn't enough in the desert.

items.name: Insulated bottle
items.why: Hot coffee at the overlook or cold water at noon.
